scope: Phase 3 claim (a) actual-413 sharing with independent expected coverage; (b) ready-gate, source/barrier and result-lease enforcement (FileWalk last-consumer retirement, derived_barrier and distinct_gate controls). Accepted deferrals: RowSemantics ops 2-9 and Rows/Hosted route controls (ryo-c01b, Phase 5); cross-rule Extend dedup Calls(2) (Phase 5); test-only lease_any (ryo-74uu).

findings.failure: The only production caller (core) always runs observations Required + capture enabled, so every rule owes Deliveries(2) and calls rule() then capture_frontiers(). No lifetime control uses a capture intent (all fixtures are CaptureIntent::Disabled). Mutating usize::from(capture != Disabled) to 0 passes every lifetime test yet releases batches after rule() and before capture_frontiers() in production. A refused wrong-entry-point call (rule() on a Forwarded rule returns NotRun at rule/service.rs:50, still decrementing) consumes the debt, and retry of a cancelled Forwarded delivery after retirement is untested.
findings.required_enforcement: Lifetime control on the production intent shape (Collected or Disabled diagnostic, observations Required, capture enabled): batch retained after rule(), released after capture_frontiers(), pass count 1. Control that a refused misuse call does not consume a delivery (or a typed per-entry-point obligation). Retry-after-retirement control asserting outcome and pass counter.

findings.failure: Retirement is relation-keyed (!pending.contains(&identity.relation)), but every lifetime fixture has one relation (LanguageTarget) and one class (all heads compare GreaterThan 1). The mutations 'release only when owed is empty' and 'class-keyed pending' both survive. A shared-source-relation batch with two classes, one still owed by another rule, is never tested, and neither is partial release of relation A while a rule owing relation B remains.
findings.required_enforcement: Fixture with two relations and two distinct classes on one relation. Assert A's batch retires while B is owed, and that the shared-relation batch stays while a distinct-class consumer still owes.

findings.failure: The row is checked [x] for 'actual413 sharing with independent expected coverage', but the ruff proof covers only heads reached on two small files (the test says so at :212-214). For the 413 program, the shared/barrier split and observed.heads come from the same walk census (shared_walk_class), so the check is self-consistency. The independent expected() runs only on the synthetic corpus. shared_cohort (>1 class in one dispatch) does not show that any class is shared by two or more rules. P3.12 stays unchecked, so the [x] overstates the evidence.
findings.required_enforcement: Apply the catalog-independent expected() to the compiled 413 program (expected heads == census shared heads, plus a removed-head negative). Emit rule membership per class and assert that one class or cohort spans two or more rules. Otherwise uncheck the row and scope it to reached heads.
